examples.en: I packed some reading material for the train.
This magazine has a lot of interesting things to read.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때는 가벼운 읽을거리가 필요해요.
examples.en: I need something light to read when I travel.
There was nothing to read in the hospital waiting room.

examples.ko: 아이에게 읽을거리 좀 사 주려고 해요.
examples.en: I am going to buy my child something to read.
Let me tell you about a website with plenty to read.

explain: 책, 잡지, 기사처럼 읽을 수 있는 것을 두루 가리켜서 '책'보다 가볍게 들려요. '읽을거리가 많다/없다', '읽을거리를 챙기다'처럼 자주 써요. '볼거리', '먹을거리'와 짝으로 기억하면 쉬워요.

phrases.en: Before the trip, I looked for something to read.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍게 읽을 것을 고를 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when picking something light to read.
phrases.en_equiv: to look for something to read

phrases.example: 읽을 만한 글이 있으면 추천해 주세요.
phrases.en: If you have anything worth reading, please recommend it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '읽을거리'보다 글의 질이 괜찮다는 느낌이 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests the writing is worth the time, more than the headword does.

phrases.en: I picked a book to read on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 읽을 것이 책일 때 이렇게 구체적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more specific way to say it when what you read is a book.

explain_en: It covers anything you can read, such as books, magazines and articles, so it sounds lighter than '책'. Common patterns are '읽을거리가 많다/없다' and '읽을거리를 챙기다'. It is easy to remember together with '볼거리' and '먹을거리'.

examples.en: The lights went out, so the room is pitch dark.
I walked alone down the pitch-dark road at night.
In the dark, only the phone light was on.
It's only six in the evening and it's already dark.
When I close my eyes, everything goes black.
Thinking about the test result made me feel hopeless.

explain: 보통 '깜깜하다'로 써요. '캄캄하다'도 같은 말인데 '깜깜하다'가 더 센 느낌이에요. 소식을 전혀 모를 때 '깜깜무소식'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: to feel hopeless about the future
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떻게 해야 할지 몰라 막막할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you have no idea what to do and the future looks bleak.

explain_en: It is usually used as '깜깜하다'. '캄캄하다' means the same, but '깜깜하다' feels stronger. When you hear nothing at all, people say '깜깜무소식'.

en: piece of wood; wood chip; splinter

examples.en: Pieces of wood are scattered on the floor.
The child made a little boat out of a piece of wood.

examples.ko: 나뭇조각에 손이 찔릴 수 있으니 장갑을 끼세요.
examples.en: Wood pieces can prick your hands, so wear gloves.
The workshop collects leftover wood pieces and sells them.
I picked up some wood scraps to use as kindling.
Splinters of wood fell off the broken chair leg.

explain: 나무가 깨지거나 잘려서 생긴 작은 조각이에요. 좀 더 굵고 덩어리진 것은 '나무토막'이라고 해요. 앞말이 모음으로 끝나고 뒤에 센소리가 오면 사이시옷을 붙여 쓴다는 점도 맞춤법에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I picked up pieces of wood on the beach and brought them home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닥에 떨어진 작은 나무 조각을 모을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for collecting small wood pieces lying around.
phrases.en_equiv: to pick up a piece of wood

phrases.en: A wood splinter was stuck in my finger and it hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 작은 나무 가시가 박힐 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used when a splinter gets stuck in the skin.

phrases.en: I made a doll out of a small piece of wood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작은'을 앞에 붙여 크기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 작은 in front to describe the size.

explain_en: A small broken fragment, like a splinter or shaving. It means a small piece broken or cut off from wood. A thicker, chunkier piece is called '나무토막'. The 사이시옷 (ㅅ) in the spelling is also a common point in Korean spelling lessons.

t90.ax: Pieces of wood are scattered on the floor.

examples.en: There is a wide swamp behind the village.
If you fall into a swamp, it's hard to get out by yourself.
Rare birds live in this swamp.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 길이 늪처럼 변했어요.
examples.en: With so much rain, the road turned into a bog.
There are so many mosquitoes near the swamp.
People gathered to protect the wetland.

explain: '늪'은 땅이 질고 물이 고여서 깊이 빠지는 곳이에요. '습지'는 물기가 많은 땅 전체를 부르는 더 넓은 말이에요. '게임의 늪', '빚의 늪'처럼 빠져나오기 어려운 상황을 비유해서도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 게임의 늪에 빠져서 공부를 못 했어요.
phrases.en: get stuck in a hole you can't climb out of
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 습관이나 상황에 깊이 빠져서 나오기 어려울 때 써요. '빚의 늪', '게임의 늪'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone sinks into a bad habit or situation and cannot get out, as in '빚의 늪' or '게임의 늪'.

explain_en: A '늪' is wet, muddy ground where you sink deeply. '습지' is the wider term for any waterlogged land. It is also used metaphorically for situations that are hard to escape, as in '빚의 늪'.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 단풍나무 잎이 빨갛게 변해요.
examples.en: When fall comes, the maple leaves turn red.

examples.ko: 공원에 단풍나무가 길을 따라 서 있어요.
examples.en: Maple trees stand along the path in the park.
We took lots of photos under the maple tree.

examples.ko: 우리 집 앞 단풍나무는 해마다 더 커져요.
examples.en: The maple tree in front of our house gets bigger every year.

examples.ko: 아이들이 단풍나무 잎을 주워서 책 사이에 끼웠어요.
examples.en: The kids picked up maple leaves and tucked them between book pages.

examples.ko: 단풍나무 한 그루가 마당을 환하게 만들어요.
examples.en: A single maple tree brightens up the yard.

explain: '단풍'은 가을에 붉거나 노랗게 물든 잎을 말하고, '단풍나무'는 손바닥처럼 갈라진 잎이 가을에 붉게 물드는 나무예요. 은행나무처럼 노랗게 물드는 나무에도 '단풍이 들다'라고 말해요. 가을 나들이는 '단풍 구경'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 단풍나무 잎을 책 사이에 끼워 뒀어요.
phrases.en: I pressed a maple leaf between the pages of a book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무 이름 뒤에 '잎'을 붙여서 잎 모양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'leaf' after the tree name lets you talk about the leaf itself.

phrases.en: We took photos under the maple tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 나타내는 조사와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is often used with a particle that marks a place.

phrases.en: I went to see the autumn leaves with my family on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무 이름이 아니라 가을에 물든 잎을 보러 가는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to going out to see autumn foliage, not the tree itself.

explain_en: '단풍' refers to leaves that turn red or yellow in autumn, while '단풍나무' is the maple, whose palm-shaped leaves turn red. Trees like ginkgo that turn yellow also take '단풍이 들다'. An autumn outing is called '단풍 구경'.

examples.en: It was raining, so I went out in a raincoat.
The yellow raincoat suits the child well.
I carry a raincoat in my bag.

examples.ko: 우산 대신 우비를 입으면 손이 자유로워요.
examples.en: If you wear a raincoat instead of using an umbrella, your hands are free.
Pack a raincoat too when you go on a picnic.

examples.ko: 그 우비는 바람이 불어도 안 젖어요.
examples.en: That raincoat doesn't get wet even in the wind.

explain: '우비'와 '비옷'은 거의 같은 말인데, 아이들 이야기에서는 '우비'가 더 자주 나와요. 우산 대신 입으면 두 손을 쓸 수 있어서 어린이나 자전거 탈 때 많이 입어요. 우산은 '쓰다', 우비는 '입다'로 동사가 달라요.

phrases.en: It rained a lot, so I took a raincoat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우비'와 거의 같은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same word as 우비.

phrases.en: I wear a raincoat when I ride a bicycle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우산은 '쓰다', 우비는 '입다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: You use 입다 with a raincoat, unlike 쓰다 with an umbrella.

phrases.en: Children's raincoats come in pretty colors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이들이 입는 우비를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for raincoats that kids wear.

explain_en: '우비' and '비옷' are nearly the same word, but '우비' comes up more often when talking about children. It frees both hands, so kids and cyclists wear it a lot. The verbs differ: you 쓰다 an umbrella, but 입다 a raincoat.

examples.en: I climbed a mountain and saw the Milky Way for the first time.

examples.ko: 맑은 날 밤하늘에는 은하수가 선명하게 보여요.
examples.en: On a clear night, the Milky Way is clearly visible in the sky.

examples.ko: 도시에서는 불빛 때문에 은하수가 안 보여요.
examples.en: In the city, you can't see the Milky Way because of the lights.
The children made wishes while looking at the Milky Way.
The photographer went far away to shoot the Milky Way.
Camping under the Milky Way was really romantic.

explain: 은하수는 밤하늘에 하얀 강처럼 길게 보이는 별 무리예요. 이름에 '물 수'가 들어가서 '은빛 강'이라는 느낌이 있고, 옛 이야기인 견우와 직녀가 건너지 못한 강이 바로 은하수예요. 영어와 달리 우유가 아니라 강으로 상상했어요.

phrases.en: You can see the Milky Way well in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밤하늘이 어두운 곳에서 볼 수 있다는 말에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for places where the night sky is dark enough to see it.

phrases.en: My friend took a photo of the Milky Way for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 은하수를 찍은 사진을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a photo taken of the Milky Way.

phrases.en: The Milky Way in the night sky is really beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밤하늘'과 함께 쓰면 장면이 더 잘 그려져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairing it with 밤하늘 makes the scene easier to picture.
phrases.en_equiv: the Milky Way in the night sky

explain_en: The visible band of stars in the night sky, everyday word. 은하수 is the long band of stars that looks like a white river across the night sky. The name contains 水, meaning water, giving a "silver river" feeling, and the river that the lovers in the old tale of 견우 and 직녀 could not cross is the 은하수. Unlike English "Milky Way," Koreans imagined a river, not milk.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 숨을 쉬면 하얀 입김이 나와요.
examples.en: In winter, a white breath cloud comes out when you breathe.
It was cold, so I blew warm breath on my numb hands.

examples.ko: 거울에 입김을 불고 손가락으로 글씨를 썼어요.
examples.en: I breathed on the mirror and wrote with my finger.
It's a cold morning when you can see your breath.

examples.ko: 아이가 창문에 입김을 불어서 그림을 그렸어요.
examples.en: The child breathed on the window and drew a picture.
My glasses fogged up because of my breath.

explain: 입김은 입에서 나온 숨이 찬 공기에서 하얗게 보이는 것이에요. 추울 때 '입김이 나다'나 '입김을 불다'로 말해요. '숨'은 몸 안의 공기이고, 눈에 보이는 입김은 겨울에 주로 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: to have a lot of influence
phrases.nuance_ko: 말 한마디로 결정에 영향을 줄 만큼 힘이 있다는 뜻으로 써요. 사람의 영향력을 말할 때 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone whose word can sway decisions; it describes a person's clout.

explain_en: 입김 is the white cloud your breath makes in cold air; you say 입김이 나다 or 입김을 불다. 숨 is the air in your body, while 입김 is the visible breath you mostly see in winter.

examples.en: It rained and the playground turned into mud.
The children played happily in the mud.
My shoes got dirty from walking on the muddy road.
The car is stuck in the mud and won't move.
I took a detour to avoid the mud.
I was surprised to see the road turned to mud.

explain: '진흙'은 흙 자체이고, '진흙탕'은 진흙이 가득한 길이나 웅덩이까지 넓게 가리켜요. '흙탕물'은 흙이 섞여 흐려진 물이에요. '진흙탕에 빠지다', '진흙탕이 되다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 두 회사의 가격 경쟁이 진흙탕 싸움이 됐어요.
phrases.en: The price competition between the two companies became a dirty fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 나쁜 방법까지 써서 지저분하게 다투는 모습을 비유해요. 보통 '진흙탕 싸움'이라는 덩어리로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor for a messy fight where both sides use dirty tactics. It is usually used as the fixed phrase.

explain_en: 진흙 is the mud itself, while 진흙탕 also covers a road or pit full of mud. 흙탕물 is water clouded by soil. It is often used as '진흙탕에 빠지다' and '진흙탕이 되다'.

t90.ax: I took a detour to avoid the mud.

en: to be prepared; to resolve; to brace oneself

examples.en: I resolved to see it through to the end.
I'm prepared for hard times ahead.
I went into the exam hall with a resolved mind.
It's fine to take on a challenge even braced for failure.
This time I practiced with the resolve to win.
I started working, bracing for overtime.

explain: 각오하다는 어려운 일이나 나쁜 결과가 있어도 받아들이고 해내겠다고 마음을 정하는 거예요. '결심하다'는 하기로 마음먹는 것이고, 각오하다는 힘든 일을 견딜 마음까지 포함해요. '각오를 하다', '각오가 되어 있다'처럼도 써요.

phrases.en: I went ready to accept that I might fail the test.
phrases.nuance_ko: '각오하다'를 '각오를 하다'로 풀어서 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spread-out form of 각오하다.

phrases.example: 저는 어려운 일도 할 각오가 되어 있어요.
phrases.en: I am ready to do even difficult things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 마음의 준비가 끝난 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state where you are already mentally ready.

phrases.en: Training gets hard from tomorrow, so be prepared.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 일이 올 테니 마음의 준비를 하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A warning to get ready for something hard.

explain_en: Steeling oneself for hardship or difficulty ahead. 각오하다 is to make up your mind to accept something hard or a bad outcome and see it through. '결심하다' is deciding to do something, while 각오하다 also includes being ready to endure the difficulty. It also appears as '각오를 하다' and '각오가 되어 있다'.

t90.ax: I'm prepared for hard times ahead.

en: to keep; to store; to treasure

examples.en: I still keep my grandmother's letter.
I will treasure this photo for the rest of my life.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 받은 인형을 소중히 간직해요.
examples.en: I carefully keep the doll I got as a child.

examples.ko: 좋은 추억을 간직해서 힘들 때 꺼내 봐요.
examples.en: I hold on to good memories and take them out when things are hard.

examples.ko: 간직하는 물건이 너무 많아서 집이 좁아요.
examples.en: I keep so many things that my house feels cramped.
I kept those words in my heart for a long time.

explain: '보관하다'는 물건을 안전하게 두는 것이고, '간직하다'는 소중해서 오래 가지고 있겠다는 마음이 들어 있어요. 편지와 사진 같은 물건뿐 아니라 추억, 말, 사랑 같은 마음에도 써요.

phrases.en: I want to keep the memories of the trip for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 아니라 마음속 추억을 소중히 가지고 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for treasuring memories in your heart, not physical objects.

phrases.en: I will keep those words in my heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들은 말이나 감정을 잊지 않고 가지고 있겠다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means you will hold on to words or feelings and not forget them.

phrases.en: I kept the letter in a drawer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소중한 물건을 잃어버리지 않게 잘 넣어 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you put a precious item away carefully so it won't get lost.

explain_en: Keep something dear in the heart or a drawer, like a letter or memory. '보관하다' is just storing something safely, while 간직하다 carries the feeling of holding on because it is precious. It fits objects like letters and photos, and also memories, words and feelings.

gh: look after valuables so nothing's lost

p.n: 보관하다 only says the letter was stored; 간직하다 adds emotional value.

t90.ax: I still keep my grandmother's letter.

en: to make an excuse; to justify

examples.en: He keeps making excuses for being late.
I made an excuse for not doing my homework.
Please do not make excuses and tell me honestly.

examples.ko: 실수를 변명할 시간에 고치는 게 나아요.
examples.en: It is better to fix a mistake than to spend time excusing it.
The child looked at me with an excuse-making face.
I understand the urge to make excuses.

explain: 자기 잘못을 가리려고 이유를 댈 때 쓰기 때문에 보통 안 좋게 들려요. 이유를 차분히 알릴 때는 '설명하다'가 어울려요. 명사 '핑계'도 비슷해서 '핑계를 대다'로 써요.

phrases.en: He made an excuse for being late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 '변명하다'와 뜻이 같고, '을/를'을 넣어 풀어 쓴 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 변명하다, written with the noun and 하다 separated.

phrases.en: Please stop making excuses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 핑계를 그만하라고 말할 때 쓰는 부정 명령이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command telling someone to stop making excuses.

phrases.en: My friend used being busy as an excuse.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변명하다'와 비슷하지만 어떤 일을 피하려고 이유를 만들 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 변명하다, but often used for inventing a reason to avoid something.

explain_en: Give reasons for your behavior; neutral, can sound like justifying. It means giving reasons to cover your own fault, so it usually sounds negative. To calmly explain a reason, '설명하다' fits better. The noun '핑계' is similar, used as '핑계를 대다'.

t90.ax: I understand the urge to make excuses.

examples.en: Smile when the photo is taken.
The staff at that shop are always smiling.
I baked smiley-shaped cookies.

examples.ko: 아침에 거울 보고 스마일 연습을 해요.
examples.en: In the morning I practice smiling in the mirror.
I drew a smiley at the end of the letter.
The smile campaign brightened up the school.

explain: 영어 smile을 그대로 쓴 말이라 '웃음'이나 '미소'보다 가볍고 귀여운 느낌이에요. 광고, 캠페인, 사진 찍을 때, 이모티콘에서 자주 쓰고 일반 문장에서는 '웃다', '미소'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I sent a smiley emoticon in the message.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃는 얼굴 그림을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the smiling face icon.

phrases.en: The baby smiled when it saw me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일반 문장에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more natural expression in ordinary sentences.

phrases.en: Smile widely when you take the photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입을 크게 벌려 환하게 웃는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes smiling brightly and widely.

explain_en: It is the English word smile used as is, so it feels lighter and cuter than 웃음 or 미소. You see it in ads, campaigns, photo moments, and emoticons; in ordinary sentences 웃다 or 미소 is more natural.

en: to control oneself; to restrain oneself; to refrain

examples.en: For my health, I'm holding back on late-night snacks.
Even when you're angry, you have to control what you say.

examples.ko: 공연 중에는 사진 촬영을 자제해 주세요.
examples.en: Please refrain from taking photos during the performance.

examples.ko: 그는 웃음을 자제하지 못하고 크게 웃었어요.
examples.en: He couldn't hold back his laughter and laughed loudly.
A notice came out telling people to avoid unnecessary outings.

examples.ko: 쇼핑을 자제한 덕분에 돈을 모을 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to cutting back on shopping, I was able to save money.

explain: 하고 싶은 것을 스스로 참고 줄일 때 써요. '참다'보다 이성적이고 부드러워서 안내문이나 부탁에 많이 나와요. '자제해 주세요'는 '하지 마세요'보다 공손하게 부탁할 때 써요.

phrases.en: Please keep your voice down here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 부탁에서 공손하게 하지 말라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in notices and requests to politely ask someone not to do something.

phrases.example: 비가 많이 와서 외출을 자제하고 있어요.
phrases.en: It's raining a lot, so I'm limiting going out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나가는 일을 스스로 줄인다는 뜻으로 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing meaning to cut down on going out by one's own choice.

phrases.en: I was angry and couldn't control my emotions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음을 누르고 조절한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to hold back and control your feelings.

explain_en: Deliberately cut back on a habit or behavior for a reason. It means holding yourself back from something you want to do. It sounds more rational and softer than 참다 (endure), so it is common in notices and polite requests. 자제해 주세요 is a gentler way to say please don't.
